name: Italian
modelReview: built 2026-11-13 by Claude Fable 5.2 from usage notes written in Italian with no knowledge of cron, a rule book derived from them, the lexicon and the visible paradigms, after two schedule reads and five blind fluency reads of the rows and seven author passes; the renderer was built by an agent that saw no other renderer and no held-out row: 152 of 153 held-out rows passed on the first judged run, and the one that failed was the row's fault (a nearest working day beside Monday to Friday adds nothing; the row was corrected). After the build, coverage found a pattern family no row had covered (every second, or one second, through minutes that are two cadences together, and a run that follows a cadence): one output printed an object and others said the wrong schedule; rows were written first and the renderer repaired by kind of part. The builder also listed about twenty places where the rule book was silent and it chose a general rule. The four sentence forms changed after the last blind read, and the built output beyond the rows, have had no independent read; no blind recovery has been run; 2026-11-13: says when both day fields must match (a day field written from a star beside a restricted one, as in Vixie cron), in rows, rule and renderer written by Claude Sonnet 5.5 from this rule book's seed and reviewed by Claude Fable 5.2; a blind Sonnet reader told these sentences from the union's 16 times of 16, and none has had a blind fluency read; 2026-11-13: hours named as numbers that are a cadence of more than eight are said by their first three «e così via fino a» the last, not one by one, in rows, rule and renderer written by Claude Opus 5.5, after a blind native reader misread a first form that bracketed listed minutes in windows; the new form has had no blind read; 2026-11-14: on the maintainer's rulings, hours that tile the day are said bare («ogni 2 ore», «ogni 6 ore», no window, no list of times, no «tutti i giorni»), or from their start when it is later («ogni 2 ore a partire dall'1:00»); a minute or second over them is said apart before a comma («al minuto 30, ogni 2 ore»), and a unit that fills each such hour is «per un'ora ogni N ore»; cadences that do not tile keep both ends. No bracket of a number series existed in Italian, so none was removed. The rule book was amended and every affected row rewritten by hand before the renderer changed, by Claude Opus 5.5 on 2026-11-14; nothing was blind-read; later the same day, on the coordinator's extension, such a cadence less an hour or two is the same cadence said bare, with the hours left out after it («ogni 2 ore, tranne alle 8:00»; «ogni minuto per un'ora ogni 2 ore, tranne dalle 8:00 alle 8:59»), again rows by hand first, by Claude Opus 5.5; nothing was blind-read; later on 2026-11-14, on the coordinator's direction: seconds named at minute 0 are counted from the hour («15 secondi dopo l'ora in punto, ogni 2 ore», «30 secondi dopo ogni ora in punto»), and every other hour under a finer field is the even or odd hours («ogni minuto nelle ore pari»), «per un'ora ogni N ore» staying for longer intervals; rule book and rows by hand first, then the renderer, by Claude Opus 5.5; nothing was blind-read; and, last on 2026-11-14: an exception never removes a cadence's first or last value (the set is said as it is, which also fixed «ogni 2 mesi a partire da febbraio tranne a febbraio»), and a cadence of seconds that tiles the minute from 0 is said by its rate («ogni 10 secondi durante il minuto 0 di ogni ora»); rows by hand first, by Claude Opus 5.5; nothing was blind-read; 2026-11-14, released stable on the full reading check: all 724 rows read by three Sonnet 5.5 readers briefed only in the language (5350 questions about moments, scored against an answer key that shares no code with the library), and each of the 10 questions most readers got wrong asked again alone of three Sonnet 5.5 and three Opus 5.5 readers: none was still misread by most readers of both (tooling/scripts/reading/recheck.mjs)
